metadata.title: CTL pharmacology evidence upgrade (selected original entries)
metadata.purpose: Evidence-driven updates to an existing 333-entry fictional game catalogue. These are not product specifications or medication instructions.
metadata.entry_match_policy: Use original_id when stored; otherwise use manual name/alias mapping. Do not auto-create titles when match is missing; some entries were skipped as duplicates by Claude Code.
metadata.merge_policy: Do not discard older material automatically; review discrepancies. Keep separate mechanism evidence vs clinical-effects evidence, and distinguish studies of pure compounds, standardized extracts, and multi-ingredient products.
metadata.scientific_limitations: This is a selected source-backed research upgrade, not comprehensive verification of all 333 original entries. Study amounts describe exposures only and are not guidance for use.
special_notes: Flmodafinil HAS a 2026 human analytical PK study; it does NOT establish human dopamine-transporter occupancy or cognition efficacy.
2024 human-receptor cell study directly challenges casual assertion that DMAA/DMHA/DMBA are direct adrenergic agonists at reachable exposures.
Large 2020 kava RCT null despite smaller 2013 positive trial.
Mesembrenone isolate evidence is not interchangeable with whole kanna-extract trials.
R vs S phenylpiracetam should not be collapsed into racemate pharmacology.
GABA-A modulation of isolated magnolol/honokiol does not prove clinical effect of highly concentrated oral supplements.
metadata.references: All evidence URLs are per-record and were located via web research on 2026-11-18.

patches.original_name: Caffeine (anhydrous, citrate, dicaffeine malate / Infinergy, PureEnergy caffeine–pterostilbene co-crystal)

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Adenosine A1 and A2A receptor antagonism explains usual CNS effects; not direct dopamine D1/D2 agonism.
research_update.reported_effects: Improves vigilance and subjective alertness; anxiety, insomnia and tremor can occur.
research_update.research_exposure: 200 mg oral caffeine vs placebo in two small randomized crossover experiments (n=8 and n=10).
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Standalone human caffeine intervention.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Response and tolerance vary; caffeine in guarana/guayusa/coffee is the same molecule, while source plants differ.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Sympathomimetic stimulant. A 2024 receptor panel found no meaningful activation of tested human alpha/beta adrenoceptors by 1,3-DMAA at concentrations up to 300 µM; weak partial TAAR1 activity only at 300 µM is unlikely physiologically relevant. Monoamine transporter involvement is a hypothesis, not proven human occupancy.
research_update.reported_effects: Human isolated study measured PK and vitals, not euphoria or improved cognition. Serious cardiovascular events have been reported in real-world exposure, often with coingredients.
research_update.research_exposure: Single oral 25 mg in 8 men (7 analyzed): mean half-life 8.45 ± 1.9 h, plasma peak at 3–5 h; no meaningful acute resting-vital change in this small study.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Single ingredient in PK study; separately marketed in multi-stimulant blends.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Tiny controlled sample does not negate case reports, establish low-dose safety, or establish recreational/euphoric effects.
research_update.target_evidence: direct in-vitro receptor panel / no verified human receptor occupancy

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Octodrine/DMHA is an alkylamine. In the 2024 human-receptor cell panel, tested dimethylhexylamine showed no alpha/beta-adrenoceptor agonism up to 300 µM and only weak TAAR1 activity at 300 µM; indirect monoamine effects are unconfirmed.
research_update.reported_effects: Stimulation frequently claimed from multi-stimulant supplements; isolated oral human psychoactive efficacy remains unestablished.
research_update.research_exposure: No verified controlled isolated human oral efficacy or dose-response study in sources reviewed.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Mainly combination products; reports cannot distinguish effects of DMHA from caffeine/yohimbine or other actives.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Trade labels and isomers can be ambiguous. Do not present claimed alpha-adrenergic receptor subtype selectivity as measured in humans.
research_update.target_evidence: direct in-vitro receptor panel for specified analogues
research_update.human_effect_evidence: no controlled human effect evidence established

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: 1,3-DMBA alkylamine: 2024 panel observed no tested human alpha/beta-adrenoceptor agonism to 300 µM and weak TAAR1 response only at 300 µM; does not establish lack of indirect activity.
research_update.reported_effects: Marketing describes stimulant effects but isolated human efficacy is undemonstrated.
research_update.research_exposure: No validated standalone oral clinical dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Found in combination products and analytical testing.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not transfer DMAA pharmacokinetics or safety data to DMBA.
research_update.target_evidence: direct in-vitro assay; functional relevance unclear

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: 1,4-DMAA (2-amino-5-methylhexane) is a distinct chemical/isomeric label; validated receptor subtype, transporter occupancy, and clinical PK are not established.
research_update.reported_effects: No independently established isolated human effects.
research_update.research_exposure: No validated human oral clinical dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Usually described on product labels or analytical reports, often with caffeine and other actives.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not merge with 1,3-DMAA or 1,5-DMHA; published tests of those do not prove this isomer acts identically.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: N,N-dimethylphenethylamine (marketed as Eria): a 2024 cell-based receptor panel measured dimethylphenethylamine weak partial α1B/α1D activation (EC50 ~6.1/8.4 µM) and TAAR1 activation (EC50 ~21 µM); exact formulation identity should be confirmed before assigning results.
research_update.reported_effects: Brief euphoria/energy claims in blends have no credible isolated clinical demonstration.
research_update.research_exposure: No established single-compound human psychoactive dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Primarily multi-stimulant products; no clean attribution.
research_update.interpretation_limits: In-vitro potency is not human receptor occupancy or demonstrated pleasant subjective response; commercial Eria label does not prove contents.
research_update.target_evidence: human receptor cell assay, formulation equivalence uncertain

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: p-Synephrine activated human α1A/α1B/α1D and β1 receptors in a 2024 cell panel, but at micromolar concentrations far above concentrations observed with common human oral intakes; clinical relevance cannot be inferred directly.
research_update.reported_effects: No convincing isolated human euphoric/cognitive profile; human cardiovascular studies of mixes confounded by caffeine and other agents.
research_update.research_exposure: Published human oral studies described 20–50 mg p-synephrine; NOT established receptor-engaging or psychoactive dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Human intake studies plus cell assays; commercial products generally contain other stimulants.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not present in-vitro α-receptor affinity as evidence of strong α agonism at ordinary human exposure.
research_update.target_evidence: human receptor cell assay; limited exposure bridging

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Oxilofrine / methylsynephrine activated β1 and α1A in human receptor cell models (EC50 ~25 µM and ~44 µM, respectively); it was not a TAAR1 agonist at concentrations up to 300 µM.
research_update.reported_effects: Sympathomimetic effects plausible; isolated standardized human CNS profile poorly studied.
research_update.research_exposure: No validated modern isolated clinical psychoactive dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Mostly found in combination pre-workouts and historical drug formulations.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not confuse oxilofrine with p-synephrine; chemically and pharmacologically distinct.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Deterenol / isopropyloctopamine acted as a relatively potent β1 agonist in the human-receptor cell assay (EC50 ~117 nM), with partial TAAR1 activation (EC50 ~1.8 µM).
research_update.reported_effects: Heart-rate stimulation is biologically plausible; standalone subjective stimulant effects and safety not clinically established.
research_update.research_exposure: No validated human oral psychoactive dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Usually supplements with multiple stimulants, not isolated trials.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Cell potency does not establish human CNS access or clinical risk magnitude.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Higenamine demonstrated β2 agonism in recombinant systems; the 2024 panel also found β1 agonism (EC50 ~34 nM) and partial β2 agonism (~0.47 µM). β2-only labeling is incomplete.
research_update.reported_effects: Cardiovascular inotropic/chronotropic effects have been observed with IV exposure; oral effects not established equivalently.
research_update.research_exposure: No justified oral psychoactive range; clinical IV exposure must not be translated into oral supplementation.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Mainly mechanistic/animal work, clinical IV heart studies, and combination supplement presence.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Human clinical IV effects and cell activity do not demonstrate oral recreational stimulation.
research_update.target_evidence: human receptor cell assay plus some physiological human IV evidence
research_update.human_effect_evidence: no controlled oral CNS effect evidence

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Yohimbine is a preferential α2-adrenoceptor antagonist, enhancing noradrenergic activity; not an α2 agonist.
research_update.reported_effects: Anxiety/panic or autonomic arousal possible, especially in panic-disorder groups; effects are not universally euphoric.
research_update.research_exposure: Oral 10/15/20 mg in 8 healthy adults; 20 mg placebo-controlled anxiety challenge in panic patients and healthy controls.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Single-drug controlled human studies exist, unlike many stimulant analogues.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Population differences important: a study in eight healthy adults found modest autonomic rather than marked anxiety effects.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Rauwolscine is a yohimbine stereoisomer and preferential α2-adrenoceptor antagonist in animal experiments; human receptor occupancy and effects are not established at commercial label exposures.
research_update.reported_effects: Autonomic stimulation/anxiety hypothesised by similarity; direct human single-compound outcomes largely absent.
research_update.research_exposure: No validated human isolated oral dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Usually combined with caffeine/synephrine; original selectivity study in anaesthetized dogs.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not substitute yohimbine human dose or effect studies for rauwolscine.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Theacrine is a purine alkaloid structurally related to caffeine; specific human receptor occupancy and a caffeine-identical adenosine mechanism are not confirmed.
research_update.reported_effects: Small studies report reduced fatigue and higher subjective energy; objective cognitive enhancement evidence is much weaker.
research_update.research_exposure: 200 mg alone vs placebo, n=15 randomized crossover (acute); open-label daily 200 or 400 mg over 7 days in n=9.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Has small standalone human trials, not merely caffeinated blend anecdotes.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Early studies often small and industry-funded; outcomes subjective, no demonstrated recreational high.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Methylliberine is a methylurate; exact human CNS receptor target/occupancy is not established.
research_update.reported_effects: Promoted for energy, but cited clinical work chiefly measures pharmacokinetics and short-term safety rather than objective mood enhancement.
research_update.research_exposure: Human trial n=125: 100 or 150 mg/day alone, or 100+50 mg / 150+25 mg with theacrine for four weeks; separate n=12 PK cocktail contained 100 mg methylliberine plus caffeine and theacrine.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Standalone arms and combination arms in a four-week safety study; cocktail PK trial cannot isolate clinical effects.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Avoid claiming randomized efficacy from a trial designed for safety.
research_update.human_effect_evidence: human safety and PK, not proven effect

patches.original_name: Modafinil (only in an older Core Labs NZT Power listing)
patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Modafinil occupies dopamine transporters in the living human brain and increases extracellular dopamine; PET demonstrated roughly 39–54% reduction in DAT ligand binding across striatal regions after 200/400 mg.
research_update.reported_effects: Wake promotion clinically established; stimulation/anxiety/insomnia possible; not simply a selective orexin agonist.
research_update.research_exposure: Ten healthy men received 200 mg and 400 mg orally in PET study; another ten-person PET study reported mean DAT occupancy 51.4% at 200 mg and 56.9% at 300 mg.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Controlled standalone human neuroimaging, plus clinical therapeutic literature.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not infer an equivalent occupancy for flmodafinil; occupancy does not itself quantify subjective euphoria.

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Flmodafinil is a fluorinated modafinil analogue; modafinil-like dopamine transporter action is plausible but direct flmodafinil human DAT occupancy has not been established.
research_update.reported_effects: No controlled clinical cognitive/alertness efficacy demonstrated by the cited 2026 experiment.
research_update.research_exposure: 2026 analytical human study: 6 volunteers each received 20 mg flmodafinil and, after washout, 20 mg fladrafinil; measured urine/dried blood spot concentrations and metabolites, not clinical benefits.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Human single-compound oral PK/excretion study, not controlled behavioral efficacy trial.
research_update.interpretation_limits: IMPORTANT CORRECTION: saying there are zero human flmodafinil studies is outdated; however, do not convert its 20 mg analytical dose to a recommended dose or infer modafinil potency.
research_update.human_effect_evidence: human metabolism evidence only; efficacy unestablished

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Phenylpiracetam is a chiral molecule: isolated R and S enantiomers have been characterized as dopamine transporter inhibitors in preclinical studies; commercial racemate must not be treated as if identical to either enantiomer.
research_update.reported_effects: Rodent metabolic/inflammatory endpoints studied; stimulant/euphoric effects in healthy humans remain poorly controlled in accessible literature.
research_update.research_exposure: R-enantiomer animal research used 50 mg/kg (mouse oral and intraperitoneal routes); no reliable transfer to human recreational doses.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Single enantiomers in laboratory animal studies, not typical marketed blends.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Avoid inferring human DAT occupancy or clean dose response from isolated R/S-enantiomer mouse findings.

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Noopept/omberacetam has experimental neuroplasticity and neuroprotection claims, but a specific clinically validated human receptor occupancy profile has not been demonstrated.
research_update.reported_effects: Some improvement reported in patients with existing neurological impairment, not proven healthy-person memory enhancement.
research_update.research_exposure: Open prospective post-stroke study described 60 patients and 20 mg/day; not a blinded healthy-volunteer efficacy experiment.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Administered alone in some Russian clinical studies; supplement anecdotes often stacked.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Nonrandomized study, clinical population and surrogate cognitive tests limit generalization.
research_update.target_evidence: preclinical mechanisms; no validated human receptor specificity

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Sunifiram (DM-235) facilitated hippocampal LTP in mouse slices via an NMDA glycine-site-sensitive, Src/PKCα/CaMKII cascade with secondary AMPAR phosphorylation; functional pathway evidence is not proof of direct NMDA ligand binding.
research_update.reported_effects: Improved scopolamine-impaired learning in rodents; no published controlled human benefit established in referenced work.
research_update.research_exposure: In vitro mouse hippocampal slices 10–100 nM LTP modulation; 0.1 mg/kg intraperitoneal in rodent memory-deficit model.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Preclinical isolated compound, no human clinical counterpart.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not label a verified direct NMDA glycine-site agonist without binding evidence; do not convert rodent doses to humans.

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: IDRA-21 is a positive modulator that reduces AMPA-receptor desensitization; pharmacology is not completely AMPA-selective and includes kainate/NMDA interactions in experimental systems.
research_update.reported_effects: Animal studies improved difficult delayed-memory performance; in patas monkeys it countered alprazolam-induced impairment, which is not the same as amplifying normal cognition.
research_update.research_exposure: Rhesus macaque oral research 0.15–10 mg/kg (individualized responses); patas monkey oral 3 or 5.6 mg/kg in alprazolam challenge. No established human dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Isolated compound tested in nonhuman primates, sometimes with alprazolam challenge.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Monkeys are not humans; long-duration behavioral findings do not establish human cognitive efficacy or safe dosing.
research_update.target_evidence: direct in vitro plus primate pharmacodynamics

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Dihexa binds hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) and promotes HGF-dependent c-Met activation in cell/rodent models; this is growth-factor signalling, not a conventional dopamine receptor agonist.
research_update.reported_effects: Rodent spatial-learning rescue and experimental synaptogenesis; no validated human cognitive effect.
research_update.research_exposure: Published preclinical cell and rodent experiments; no established safe human oral dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Isolated experimental peptide analogue in laboratory research.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Potential growth-related signalling is not proof of a clinical cancer effect; long-term safety unknown and should not be invented.

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: 9-Me-BC inhibited MAO-A (IC50 ~1 µM) more strongly than MAO-B (~15.5 µM) in biochemical assays and altered astrocytic neurotrophic gene expression.
research_update.reported_effects: Neuroprotective claims derive chiefly from cultured cells, not human mood/cognition trials.
research_update.research_exposure: Cell concentrations in µM; no verified human oral clinical dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Cell/astrocyte experiments; retail self-reports not controlled evidence.
research_update.interpretation_limits: MAO interaction raises theoretical interaction concerns; in vitro IC50 is not established in-vivo brain enzyme inhibition.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Tesofensine inhibits serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake (triple monoamine transporter blocker), not a single receptor agonist.
research_update.reported_effects: Weight loss and appetite effects in obesity trial; dry mouth, GI upset and insomnia commonly reported; raised heart rate at 0.5 mg/day.
research_update.research_exposure: 203 participants in 24-week obesity RCT: oral 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 mg/day vs placebo.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Standalone investigational drug in controlled human trial alongside an energy-restricted diet.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Trial endpoints do not establish euphoria or other recreational effects; not a supplement safety standard.

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Methylene blue is a redox-active compound and potently inhibits MAO-A (more than MAO-B) in enzyme assays. Its mitochondrial electron transport effects vary by concentration and setting.
research_update.reported_effects: Some specialized medical applications; no reliable claim that a retail oral supplement gives acute stimulant euphoria or better cognition.
research_update.research_exposure: No generalizable oral cognition dose established from cited MAO study (which was purified human-enzyme pharmacology).
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Evidence includes purified-enzyme study and medical contexts; supplement formulas do not validate target engagement.
research_update.interpretation_limits: MAO-A inhibition makes serotonergic drug interactions clinically important; cannot infer absence of risk from no immediate effects.
research_update.target_evidence: direct biochemical human MAO-A enzyme inhibition
research_update.human_effect_evidence: no clinical enhancement supported by cited assay

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Huperzine A is a reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, indirectly increasing cholinergic transmission; it is not a selective nicotinic receptor agonist.
research_update.reported_effects: Large phase-II Alzheimer study primary cognitive endpoint negative at lower studied dose; some exploratory higher-dose outcomes improved transiently.
research_update.research_exposure: 210 Alzheimer participants randomized to 200 µg twice daily, 400 µg twice daily or placebo for at least 16 weeks.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Standalone drug in controlled clinical trial, not a healthy-person nootropic validation.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Study primary outcome at 200 µg BID was null; avoid treating exploratory 11-week result as unequivocal efficacy.
research_update.human_effect_evidence: controlled patient trial with null primary endpoint

patches.original_category: Eugeroics, racetams and other synthetic nootropics

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Isolated mesembrenone inhibits SERT and PDE4 in vitro (both reported IC50 below 1 µM); effects depend on alkaloid purity and assay.
research_update.reported_effects: Standalone mesembrenone oral human mood/psychoactivity has not been established; whole-kanna RCTs do not isolate this molecule.
research_update.research_exposure: No validated human oral mesembrenone dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Mechanistic experiments on isolated alkaloid; human trials used standardized multialkaloid plant extracts.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not directly assign Zembrin clinical dose or effect to pure mesembrenone.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Kanna/Sceletium contains variable alkaloids. Mesembrine is potent in-vitro SERT inhibitor (Ki ~1.4 nM); mesembrenone additionally affects PDE4; extract activity depends on alkaloid profile.
research_update.reported_effects: Small trial of standardized Zembrin found better selected executive-function outcomes; 3-month safety trial reported tolerability. These do not prove acute recreational effects for arbitrary extracts.
research_update.research_exposure: Zembrin oral extract: 8 and 25 mg/day over 3 months (n=37 safety study), and 25 mg/day for 3 weeks (n=21 cognitive crossover).
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Human studies used standardized multi-alkaloid extract alone, not pure mesembrine and not arbitrary kanna products.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Study-specific standardized-extract doses cannot be extrapolated to 7% alkaloid concentrated retail material.
research_update.target_evidence: in-vitro compound targets; no PET occupancy

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Kava is a chemically diverse kavalactone mixture with multiple possible GABAergic/ion-channel effects; no single universally validated human benzodiazepine-site occupancy profile.
research_update.reported_effects: 2013 6-week randomized GAD trial found significant reduction in anxiety, while larger 2020 16-week trial did not outperform placebo.
research_update.research_exposure: 2013 trial 120–240 mg kavalactones/day (n=75 enrolled); 2020 trial 120 mg kavalactones twice daily (n=171).
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Isolated standardized aqueous kava extract in randomized trials.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Conclusions mixed; kavalactone amount is not the same as mass of crude kava root or extract, and quality/preparation affect safety.
research_update.target_evidence: multiple preclinical pathways, clinical receptor occupancy unknown

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Magnolol and honokiol positively allosterically modulate synaptic and extrasynaptic GABA-A receptors in neurons/recombinant systems, with particularly high efficacy in delta-containing receptors; not equivalent to a classical benzodiazepine-site ligand.
research_update.reported_effects: Human relief-of-stress claims principally use combinations; isolated highly concentrated magnolol/honokiol psychoactivity is not established in controlled human trials.
research_update.research_exposure: In one 6-week pilot RCT, 250 mg Relora (Magnolia + Phellodendron mixture) three times daily, n=40 recruited; not comparable to pure magnolol/honokiol dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: In-vitro/neuronal isolated compounds; human trial of 2-botanical blend.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Do not infer human exposure to isolated magnolol/honokiol or direct additivity with GABAergic sedatives from combination trial.
research_update.human_effect_evidence: human effect confounded by multi-herb formulation

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: L-theanine glutamate-related and neurophysiologic effects are reported, but no established high-affinity single human CNS receptor occupancy accounts for its clinical effects.
research_update.reported_effects: Small placebo-controlled crossover trial reported improvements in some stress, sleep and cognitive test scores after daily administration.
research_update.research_exposure: 200 mg/day oral for 4 weeks in a 30-person randomized crossover trial.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Standalone controlled human intervention, also present in many caffeine combinations.
research_update.interpretation_limits: A moderate stress-score change is not evidence of an intense acute sedative or recreational effect.

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: 5-HTP is a serotonin biosynthetic precursor converted by aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase; not itself a serotonin-receptor agonist. Peripheral conversion and GI serotonin complicate effects.
research_update.reported_effects: In a 2026 blinded acute trial of 112 adults selected by ADHD-trait levels, no significant benefit on measured distractibility; 19.6% of active participants reported fatigue, nausea, or vomiting.
research_update.research_exposure: Single oral 200 mg 5-HTP vs placebo with tasks repeated after 90 minutes; no validated acute recreational dose.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Isolated 5-HTP/placebo trial.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Serotonergic interaction risk; a negative attention trial does not settle depression indication and dose does not prove central serotonin concentrations.
research_update.human_effect_evidence: human controlled null cognition, adverse events

research_update.target_or_receptor_profile: Melatonin activates MT1/MT2 receptors (chronobiotic hormone); mechanism differs from direct GABA-A sedatives.
research_update.reported_effects: Can shift circadian timing and modestly improve sleep initiation; effects depend substantially on administration time.
research_update.research_exposure: 2024 meta-analysis of 26 double-blind RCTs (1,689 observations) found modeled sleep effects peaking around 3–5 mg/day; not a claim that high doses produce extra sedation.
research_update.alone_vs_combination: Human single-agent randomized trials synthesized in meta-analysis; some combinations exist.
research_update.interpretation_limits: Dose-effect curve and timing are context-specific; product labels of 10 mg do not imply greater benefit.
